recommendations.recommendation: Aim for tiny improvements each day, since small changes compound into large results over time.
recommendations.rationale: Small gains multiply like compound interest, so consistency outweighs dramatic one-off efforts.
recommendations.argued_against: Waiting for big breakthroughs or expecting instant results

recommendations.recommendation: Focus on systems and daily processes rather than on goals alone.
recommendations.rationale: Goals set direction but systems produce progress; winners and losers share the same goals.

recommendations.recommendation: Build habits around the kind of person you want to be, not only the outcomes you want.
recommendations.rationale: Lasting change comes when a habit becomes part of your self-image, and each repetition votes for that identity.

recommendations.recommendation: Make a desired habit obvious by noticing cues and writing down a specific plan for when and where you will do it.
recommendations.rationale: Behavior is triggered by cues in the environment; clear plans remove reliance on motivation.

recommendations.recommendation: Stack a new habit onto an existing routine so the old one triggers the new one.
recommendations.rationale: Existing habits give a ready-made trigger for a new behavior.

recommendations.recommendation: Redesign your surroundings so good cues are visible and bad cues are hidden.
recommendations.rationale: Environment shapes behavior more than willpower does.

recommendations.recommendation: Make habits attractive by pairing them with something you enjoy and joining groups where the habit is normal.
recommendations.rationale: People imitate those around them and act on anticipated reward.
recommendations.argued_against: Surrounding yourself with people who model unwanted habits

recommendations.recommendation: Make habits easy by reducing steps and starting with a version that takes about 2 minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Lower friction makes starting more likely, and showing up matters more than intensity at first.

recommendations.recommendation: Make good habits satisfying with immediate rewards and track them visibly, for example with a habit tracker.
recommendations.rationale: The brain favors immediate rewards, and visible progress is motivating.
recommendations.argued_against: Delayed gratification as the only reward

recommendations.recommendation: Never miss twice in a row; if you skip a day, get back on track right away.
recommendations.rationale: One lapse is harmless but repeated lapses start a new habit of not doing it.

recommendations.recommendation: Make bad habits invisible, unattractive, difficult, and unsatisfying, reversing the rules for good ones.
recommendations.rationale: Breaking a habit means inverting each step of the behavior loop.

recommendations.recommendation: Pick activities that suit your strengths and personality, and keep working at the edge of your ability.
recommendations.rationale: Tasks of just manageable difficulty keep people engaged; fit with natural talents helps sustain effort.
recommendations.conditions: Needs a suitable level of challenge to avoid boredom

recommendations.recommendation: Review your habits regularly and avoid tying your identity too rigidly to one role.
recommendations.rationale: Reflection keeps habits useful, and rigid identities make change hard when circumstances shift.
